findings.evidence: Line 216: `(pathSpan x 0).toSubmodule a = (pathSpan x 1).toSubmodule a`, hypothesis `h : a ≠ i`; lines 229/241 give `= Submodule.span k {x}` and `= ⊥` at `i`, so the unqualified `pathSpan_zero_eq_pathSpan_one` claim is not a theorem.
findings.fix: Put the projection in the name, e.g. `toSubmodule_pathSpan_zero_eq_toSubmodule_pathSpan_one_of_ne` (or the file's own prefix style: `toSubmodule_pathSpan_zero_eq_of_ne`). Same omission in `pathSpan_zero_self_of_isAcyclic` (line 228) and `pathSpan_one_self_of_isAcyclic` (line 240), whose names also drop the conclusion — `…_eq_span_singleton` / `…_eq_bot` — while the sibling `toSubmodule_pathSpan` (line 209) does name the projection.
findings.issue: `pathSpan_zero_eq_pathSpan_one_of_ne` reads as `pathSpan x 0 = pathSpan x 1`, which is false in general (the two subrepresentations differ exactly at `i` — that is the whole point of `pathSpan_zero_self_of_isAcyclic` vs `pathSpan_one_self_of_isAcyclic`). The statement only equates `.toSubmodule a` for `a ≠ i`.

findings.evidence: Line 262: `ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton k (M.obj a) (M.map (eqToHom h.symm) x))` — the morphism is determined by `x`, which the name does not mention.
findings.fix: Name it after what it does, following the `LinearMap.toSpanSingleton` it wraps: `simpleRepToSpanSingleton` (and `simpleRepToSpanSingleton_app_generator` for line 275).
findings.issue: `simpleRepHom` names a construction that depends on the chosen vector `x` as if it were the canonical morphism out of `Sᵢ`; the same file already uses "hom out of `simpleRep`" generically in `simpleRep_hom_eq_zero_iff` (line 196), so the name does not distinguish this map from any other `Sᵢ ⟶ M`.

summary: No notation is introduced, and the structure/field names follow Mathlib's `Subrepresentation` precedent. Three names are off: one advertises an equality of subrepresentations it does not prove, one breaks the repo's established `not_nonempty_…_iso_of_isAcyclic` / `exists_nonempty_…` pattern, and one gives a canonical-sounding name to an `x`-dependent morphism.
